summary: The agent completed a substantial fold-generation implementation and its own focused fixture test passed, but the hidden verifier failed at Java compilation because generated code reused the method parameter name `value` for a folded child attribute also named `value`. This is a solution integration bug in the generated API/body rather than an environment or verifier issue.
quick_failure_summary: Generated `SignalNetFold.java` does not compile due to a duplicate local variable named `value`.

details.reasoning: The Maven verifier stopped before executing tests with `/app/value-fixture/target/generated-test-sources/test-annotations/org/immutables/fixture/fold_c8b14d/SignalNetFold.java:[55,47] error: variable value is already defined in method caseLatch(Latch,R,R)`. The agent's generator emits a fold entry method with a parameter named `value`, then declares child-result locals using raw attribute names (`[p.type] [p.name] = ...`). The hidden fixture has a family attribute `Node value()` on `SignalNet.Latch`, so the generated method attempts to declare a second `value` variable in the same scope. A generated-code feature must avoid collisions with common attribute names, and the codebase commonly supports attributes called `value`; this is a structural integration failure in the implementation.
details.secondary_factors: The implementation likely had additional behavioral gaps hidden behind the compile failure, but the duplicate-name generated-code error is the first and dominant verifier failure. The agent only validated against a narrower self-authored fixture whose `value()` attribute was not a folded family child, so it missed this collision.
